title: Letter Series
tagline: Year 1 Foundation — Patterns built from alphabet positions

introduction.overview: A letter series is a list of letters or letter groups that follows a rule based on their positions in the English alphabet. The rule can move forward or backward by a fixed gap, use a gap that grows, alternate between two patterns, or work on each letter of a group separately. The key skill is to convert letters into position numbers so that the problem becomes a number series.
introduction.placementRelevance: Letter series questions are commonly asked in company reasoning rounds. They are quick to solve for a student who knows the alphabet positions well, so they are a good source of fast marks.
introduction.realWorldContext: Spreadsheet column names (A, B, … Z, AA, AB), seat numbering in a theatre and codes used in inventory labels all use alphabetical order and gaps in the same way.

learningObjectives: Recall the position of any letter quickly, from both ends of the alphabet
Convert letter patterns into number patterns
Solve series with constant, increasing and alternating gaps
Handle two-letter and three-letter groups by treating each position separately
Use the opposite-letter rule (positions add up to 27)

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: A = 1, B = 2, …, Z = 26. A useful anchor is the word EJOTY: E = 5, J = 10, O = 15, T = 20, Y = 25. Each letter and its opposite (A–Z, B–Y, …) add up to 27.

coreDefinitions: Position value: the number of a letter in the alphabet counted from A. A = 1, M = 13, Z = 26.
Opposite letter: the letter at the same distance from the other end. Position from the left + position from the right = 27.
Gap (step): the number of positions between two consecutive letters in a series.
Letter group: a block of two or more letters treated as one term, such as ACE or AZ.
Wrap-around: after Z, counting continues from A (so Z + 1 = A, Z + 2 = B). Many series do not need this, but check when a gap carries you past Z.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A letter series is a number series in disguise. Replace each letter with its number, find the rule in the numbers, then convert the answer back to a letter. For letter groups the same rule usually works separately in each position of the group, left letter against left letter and so on.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Imagine a ruler marked A to Z. Each term in the series is a point on the ruler. A constant gap means equal jumps; an increasing gap means jumps of 1, 2, 3, …; a series moving to the left means decreasing positions.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Position and opposite
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Position from left + position from right = 27
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Both counts include the letter itself.
importantRulesAndFormulas.whenToUse: Questions about the nth letter from the end.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Constant gap
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Add (or subtract) the same number each time.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Group series
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Treat each position of a group separately
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: First letters form one series, second letters another.
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: Left letters A, B, C, D, E and right letters Z, Y, X, W, V → EV

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Wrap-around
importantRulesAndFormulas.description: Alphabet is circular in some questions.

mainNarrative: Begin by writing the position number under each letter. For A, C, E, G the numbers are 1, 3, 5, 7. The rule is a constant gap of 2, so the next is 9 = I. This conversion step makes every later check an arithmetic one.
Letters can move backwards: Z, X, V, T has positions 26, 24, 22, 20 and the next is 18 = R. Look at the first two letters and decide whether the series is moving towards A or Z.
Increasing gaps give series such as A, B, D, G, K, whose positions are 1, 2, 4, 7, 11. The gaps are 1, 2, 3, 4, so the next gap is 5 and the next letter is 16 = P.
For groups such as AZ, BY, CX, DW, handle the left letters and right letters as two separate series: A, B, C, D (moving forward) and Z, Y, X, W (moving backward). The next group is EV.

In groups with three letters like ACE, FHJ, KMO, check whether each position moves by the same gap from group to group. Here every letter shifts by 5 from one group to the next (A→F→K), so the next group is PRT.

deepDiveAspects.title: Alternating letter series
deepDiveAspects.content: In a series like A, Z, B, Y, C, X the odd terms go forward (A, B, C) and the even terms go backward (Z, Y, X). Separate them, find each rule, and continue the series with the correct sub-series for the next position.

deepDiveAspects.title: Why EJOTY helps
deepDiveAspects.content: Remembering E = 5, J = 10, O = 15, T = 20, Y = 25 lets you reach any letter within two or three counts, which saves precious seconds in a timed test.

problemVariations.description: Left and right letters move separately.
Odd and even positions follow different rules.
problemVariations.exampleSnippet: A, Z, B, Y, C, X, ?

solvedExamples.title: Increasing gaps
solvedExamples.question: Find the next letter: A, B, D, G, K, ?
givenInfo: Series: A, B, D, G, K
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Convert to positions and study the gaps.

steps.title: Continue the gaps
steps.explanation: The next gap is 5, so the next position is 11 + 5 = 16.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The gaps 1, 2, 3, 4 grow by one each time, a standard pattern of increasing gaps.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Assuming a constant gap after seeing the first two letters, which gives C instead of D.

solvedExamples.title: Letter groups that move in opposite directions
solvedExamples.question: Find the next group: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?
solvedExamples.conceptOrFormula: Treat the left letters and right letters as two separate series.

steps.title: Left letters
steps.explanation: A, B, C, D go forward by 1. The next is E.

steps.title: Right letters
steps.explanation: Z, Y, X, W go backward by 1. The next is V.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Each group pairs a letter with its opposite, and the pairing shifts by one in each step.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Treating AZ as one unit and looking for a pattern in the whole group.

solvedExamples.title: Backward series with a growing gap
solvedExamples.question: Find the next letter: Z, W, S, N, H, ?
givenInfo: Series: Z, W, S, N, H

steps.title: Next gap
steps.explanation: The next gap is −7, so the position is 8 − 7 = 1.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The gaps are 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 going down the alphabet.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Forgetting that the series moves backwards and adding the gaps.

shortcutMethods.title: Convert to numbers, then use the number-series toolbox

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Count letters on your fingers from A each time you need a position.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Memorise EJOTY (5, 10, 15, 20, 25) and count only 1–2 steps from the nearest anchor. Use the opposite-letter rule for positions from the right: 27 minus the left position.

rulesForApplication: Always write the positions under the letters on the first pass.
For groups, track each position separately.
Use a "27" rule for opposite letters.
When a series moves past Z, wrap around by subtracting 26.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Counting from memory and slipping by one.
commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Use the EJOTY anchors and double-check by counting from the nearest anchor.

commonMistakes.mistake: Treating a letter group as a single item
commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Overlooking that each letter follows its own rule.
commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Split the group into columns and examine each column.
Check the first two letters: smaller to larger is forward, larger to smaller is backward.

commonMistakes.whyItHappens: Position exceeds 26 and the answer is not a letter.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Write the positions of each option and see which one fits the number pattern; wrong options usually break the gap.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Do letter series early in the reasoning section; they are among the fastest to finish.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Speed comes from remembering the anchor letters and the opposite-letter rule, not from any complex theory.

summaryBullets: Convert letters to numbers, find the gap pattern, convert back.
For groups, solve each position separately.
quickFormulas: Position from the right = 27 − position from the left

keyTakeaways: A letter series is a number series in disguise.
Look at each position of a group separately.
selfCheckQuestions: Can I give the 9th letter from the end of the alphabet?
Can I continue QPO, NML, KJI, HGF?
Can I spot the gap pattern in A, B, D, G, K, ?
